summary.title: Use GNU Emacs: The Plain Text Computing Environment
summary.one_liner: A free, online, CC BY-NC-ND book by Keith Waclena that teaches GNU Emacs 30.2 from the basics through files, search, Dired, version control, and programming.
takeaways: Emacs core concepts (buffers, windows, frames, point, mark, region, kill ring) are explained in the early chapters and are worth reading first.
Built-in features such as Dired, incremental search, file handling, shells, version control (VC), and mail are covered in depth.
The book recommends learning with minimal customization and using the built-in Emacs tutorial alongside it.
Many chapters are marked UNFINISHED; the book is a work in progress at version 30.2.29.
summary.summary: This is the online HTML edition of Keith Waclena's book on GNU Emacs, originally written around 1997 and revised for version 30.2. The table of contents covers fundamentals (concepts, key bindings, files, buffers, windows), file and directory work with Dired, searching and replacing, undo and keyboard macros, customization, and additional topics such as registers, Org Mode, shells, version control, and email. It also includes an appendix with a glossary and an optional minimal init file. The page text is the front matter and introduction, which focus on Emacs as a free, portable, extensible, self-documenting editor, and it notes that many chapters are still unfinished.
